proposal.comment: [Playbook] Array's Section 16.2 indemnity covers only Array Territory activities, Array-sponsored studies and Article 15 breaches, leaving us exposed on third-party IP claims arising from our exercise of the licensed Array Patents and Know-How. We have added a licensor IP indemnity with the usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap.

ops.text: IP Indemnification. Array shall indemnify each Ono Indemnitee against any Third Party Claim alleging that any Product or Ono's exercise of the licenses granted by Array hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party, excluding any claim arising from Ono's modifications, Ono's combinations with other products or materials, or Ono's specifications. Array shall, at its option, procure for Ono the right to continue use, modify the infringing item, or replace the infringing item, and if none of the foregoing is available, refund the amounts paid by Ono for the affected Product. Array's total liability under this Section 16.2A shall not exceed 3 times the annual fees paid by Ono under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Insert Array IP-infringement indemnity (usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3x annual fees super-cap) after Section 16.2

quote: and (d) any breach of any representations, warranties or covenants by Array in Article 15 above, except to the extent such Third Party Claims result from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of a Ono Indemnitee.
rationale: Array's indemnity in Section 16.2 is limited to Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breaches of Array's Article 15 representations; it contains no limb for third-party claims that the Products or our exercise of the licensed Array Patents/Know-How infringe or misappropriate third-party IP (and Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty), while our Section 16.1(a) indemnity covers all Third Party Claims from our Ono Territory activities. That fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a licensor IP indemnity. We take the fallback position: a single concise IP indemnity limb with the usual exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications), the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder and a 3x annual fees super-cap, which is the least intrusive cure and leaves the existing mutual architecture and Section 16.3 procedure untouched.

verification.notes: The locked fallback level is fully satisfied: a new licensor IP indemnity is inserted with all three required exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications), all four remedies in the required order (procure, modify, replace, refund) and an express 3× annual fees super-cap. Preferred level is not met (no breach-of-law, data-breach or GN/WM triggers, no express notice/control/cooperation mechanic, and no narrowing of Ono's own indemnity), but that is consistent with the drafter's locked fallback target. Minimality holds: a single concise insertion addresses an absent clause without touching Sections 16.1/16.2 or rewriting the indemnity architecture; no preferred-only elements were smuggled in. Intent preserved: the insertion uses existing defined terms ("Ono Indemnitees", "Third Party Claim", "Product", "Third Party"), is self-numbered 16.2A consistent with its internal cross-reference, and leaves all other commercial terms effective. Note for the rationale only (not a deviation): the cap is measured on fees "paid" rather than "paid or payable", and the clause says "indemnify" without an express duty to defend.

quote: (a) Title to all know-how, inventions and other intellectual property made solely by Ono personnel (or that of any Affiliate) in connection with this Agreement shall be owned by Ono (or its respective Affiliate).
rationale: The IP allocation works in our favour and no Ono IP or data is assigned to Array during the term. Section 11.1(a) gives Ono outright ownership of everything made solely by Ono personnel (Array's ownership of its own compound IP under 11.1(b) is the acceptable "vendor keeps its platform" position), Section 4.6(c) (p0329) confirms Ono owns its INDs and Marketing Approvals in the Ono Territory, Section 2.7 preserves each Party's retained rights, and Section 13.1 converts our Article II licences into perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free, sublicensable licences on expiry — which independently satisfies the fallback licence-back requirement. The outbound Grant-Back in Section 2.6 is a non-exclusive, subject-to-our-exclusivity licence of Improvements and our Joint IP interest, not an assignment, so it is not walk-away territory. Two points sit at the fallback rather than the preferred position and are noted rather than redlined: (i) Section 11.1(c) does create joint ownership of jointly-made IP, and 11.1(d) limits each Party to internal practice and requires the other Party's consent to enforce, license or assign — but the restriction is reciprocal and expressly disapplied "to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other", and our Section 2.1(a)-(c) licences cover Array's interests in the Joint Patents and Joint Know-How for Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products throughout the Ono Territory, so we retain a workable right to exploit joint IP across our whole commercial field; (ii) Sections 14.2(a)(iii) and (vii) require assignment of Product-specific Regulatory Filings and Product Trademarks on termination, but that is ordinary reversion of a licensed product (our corporate names are carved out) and, where we terminate for Array's material breach or insolvency under 13.3/13.4, Section 14.2(a)(ix) requires Array to pay market-rate consideration for those rights instead. No redline warranted.

quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise
rationale: Section 18.9 is fully mutual and contains the M&A/successor carve-out: either Party (including Ono) may assign without the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to an assumption writing. Other assignments require consent, and Affiliate assignments are permitted with consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed" — i.e., the rule's fallback consent standard, applied symmetrically to Array as well as to us. There is no Array right to terminate, re-price or otherwise exit on an Ono change of control: the only change-of-control provisions in the document (Section 18.10 and Section 4.5(b) at p0322) are triggered by a Change in Control of Array, not of Ono, and Section 18.10 imposes firewall obligations on Array's acquirer rather than granting any exit right. This sits at (and on the successor carve-out above) the fallback, so no redline. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the preferred position would allow Affiliate assignment without consent, and the proviso letting the non-assigning Party refuse consent where it reasonably believes an Affiliate assignment could cause it material adverse tax consequences is a narrow, reciprocal qualifier on a minor sub-element. We would also observe commercially (not as an assignment issue) that p0322 lets Array's Section 4.5(b) restrictions lapse on Array's own Change in Control, which is a separate non-compete point rather than a breach of this rule.

quote: (a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials
rationale: No sole-supplier or requirements-purchase obligation is imposed on us. Article IX frames supply entirely as our option: Section 9.4(a) (p0508) gives Ono the right but not the obligation to Manufacture or engage its own Subcontractor, with Know-How transfer and step-in rights; Section 9.4(b) (p0509) says Ono shall have the right to obtain commercial requirements from Array, with a Supply Agreement entered into only upon Ono's request. Section 9.1(a) (p0495) obliges Array to supply or secure supply of our requirements with no reciprocal exclusive-purchase commitment from us, and Section 9.5 (p0516) passes through the benefit of Array's Third Party supplier arrangements. Our freedom to second-source is fully preserved, meeting the preferred position. The only exclusivity binding us is Section 8.2 (p0491), a reciprocal field non-compete rather than exclusive dealing: mutual (Array and its Controlled Affiliates equally bound), limited to two defined Competing Product categories, limited to the Ono Territory, time-limited to a defined date, and the quid pro quo for the exclusive licences granted to us under Sections 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) (p0162, p0164), which benefit us and are not flagged. That covenant sits at or above the fallback; we note only that it does not expressly release us if Array itself commercialises a Competing Product (it instead ends the royalty period), a minor sub-element rather than a material failure. No redline proposed.

quote: 14.3 Liquidated Damages. In the event that Array (a) [ * ] during [ * ], or (b) intentionally conceals or falsifies a material result and/or material item of data concerning the safety or efficacy of the Product, which concealment or falsification (i) is undertaken to induce Ono to not terminate this Agreement and (ii) results in a substantial reduction to the value of the Product in the Ono Territory
rationale:
The Agreement meets the preferred position: there are no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Ono (our party). The only liquidated damages clause, Section 14.3 (p0668/p0671), runs entirely in our favour — it is triggered by Array's conduct (including intentional concealment or falsification of safety/efficacy data) and gives Ono the election to continue the Agreement with (A) relief from its own due diligence obligations and (B) a reduction in the otherwise applicable royalty rate as the liquidated amount. Per the playbook, LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant and we do not flag a clause that benefits us.

I checked the other candidates and Article VII for any Customer-payable penalty and found none: (i) p0430 is a royalty true-up/reconciliation — a shortfall of royalties actually owed on Net Sales, not a penalty or fixed damages amount; (ii) Section 7.1 (p0463) is mutual, reciprocal late-payment interest at LIBOR plus a margin on sums actually overdue, payable by whichever Party is delinquent, which is compensatory interest rather than liquidated damages; (iii) there is no early-termination fee, minimum annual royalty, forfeiture or minimum-payment-on-termination anywhere in the document (searches for "penalty", "termination fee", "minimum", "forfeit" and "minimum annual royalty" returned nothing relevant). Section 14.5 confirms only milestone and royalty payments already accrued survive termination.

One note for the record, not a deviation under this rule: Sections 14.2(a)(i) and 14.2(a)(iii) allocate the actual costs of wind-down transfers and ongoing Clinical Studies to Ono where Ono terminates for convenience under Section 13.2 or Array terminates for cause. These are reimbursements of genuine costs incurred, uncapped but not a stipulated sum, so they are cost allocation rather than a liquidated damages or penalty mechanic and fall outside this rule. No redline proposed.

quote: Ono shall have the right, in accordance with this Section 2.2, to grant sublicenses under the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates and to Third Parties, provided that Ono shall not engage a Third Party as either (i) a Sublicensee of the Product, or (ii) as a distributor of the Product, without Array's prior written consent.
rationale: The grant package meets the preferred position on every material term. Array grants Ono exclusive Development and Commercialization licences (2.1(a), (c)) and a worldwide non-exclusive Manufacturing licence (2.1(b)), and our Affiliates are covered as of right — Section 2.2(a) permits sublicensing to Affiliates without consent, and 2.1(b) is expressly sublicensable to Affiliates — which is better than the fallback's "affiliates on written notice." Contractors acting on our behalf are covered: 2.1(b) expressly allows extension to Third Party manufacturers "for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf," and the Subcontractor definition (1.57) and Articles IV/IX contemplate performance of activities through Subcontractors. Nothing is revocable at Array's discretion: Array can terminate only for uncured material breach (13.3, 90/60-day cure) or bankruptcy (13.4), while at-will termination rights sit with us (13.2, 13.5), and on expiry the Section 2.1 licences become "fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights" (13.1). Successor transfer is satisfied by Section 18.9, which permits assignment without consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of the business or assets by merger or acquisition, with the Agreement inuring to successors and permitted assigns. Two sub-elements fall short of ideal but are not material deviations and are noted only: engaging a Third Party as Sublicensee or distributor of the Product needs Array's prior written consent, and the licences exclude any right to modify Binimetinib or Encorafenib (2.1(d)) — ordinary field limits in a pharma collaboration rather than an exclusion of affiliates/contractors with no path to add them. No redline proposed.

quote: The seat of the arbitration shall be in Osaka, Japan, if it is demanded by Array, and in New York, NY, USA, if it is demanded by Ono, with hearings to held in the same location.
rationale: Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: Section 18.3 (p0765) provides that the Agreement "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States," with CISG excluded. On forum, Section 17.3 (p0747-p0748) provides mandatory ICC arbitration before three arbitrators rather than the preferred New York courts, but this does not reach walk-away territory. Walk-away is defined as the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Here neither seat option is Array's home jurisdiction (Array is a Delaware company based in Boulder, Colorado): the seat is New York, NY when Ono demands arbitration — a fully accepted venue — and Osaka, Japan when Array demands, which is our own client's home city (Ono is organized under the laws of Japan with its principal place of business in Osaka). The demand-based election is reciprocal and, in the only case where the seat falls outside the accepted list, it lands on our home turf, so that limb benefits our party and we do not flag it. Court access is also preserved: each Party retains the right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief (p0757), and either Party may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751). Noted in passing but not flagged as deviations: the forum is arbitration rather than courts, the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions are disapplied, and Section 18.3 governing law is carved out from procedural issues (p0749) — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not disadvantage us given the New York substantive law and preserved court remedies.

quote: Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array.
rationale: Searches across the standard MFN phrasings ("most favored/favoured nation", "no less favorable", "as favorable", "more favorable", "better terms", "best price", "first refusal", "match") return no clause obliging Ono to extend Array terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and no obligation to match third-party offers. The two closest analogues both run in our favour: p0502 protects Ono by barring Array from forcing direct Subcontractor orders unless the terms are as favorable to Ono as those the Subcontractors extend to Array, and p0190 requires Array to use Diligent Efforts to pass through Third Party Partner data, rights of reference and improvements to Ono without charge. The only other "favorable" reference (p0476) is a routine withholding-tax rate provision, not an MFN. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdens the Customer — so no redline is warranted; per the rule, MFN benefits flowing to us are welcome and are not flagged.

Forecasting and ordering mechanics are deferred to the future clinical and commercial Supply Agreements, so no binding volume is created here; we should ensure those agreements likewise avoid non-cancellable minimums when negotiated. The only "shortfall" reference (p0430) is a year-end royalty true-up reconciliation, not a purchase minimum. This meets the preferred position (fees for ordered supply only), so no redline is warranted.

quote: 13.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13, shall continue in full force and effect, on a Product-by-Product and country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Term with respect to such Product expires, at which time this Agreement shall expire in its entirety with respect to such Product in such country.
rationale: The auto-renewal mechanics this rule targets are not used in this agreement. Section 13.1 sets a single, self-liquidating term running from the Effective Date until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis; there is no automatic renewal, no successive renewal term, and therefore no non-renewal notice window or renewal price uplift to compute (a document-wide search for "renew"/renewal-term language returns only patent-term renewals and Section 14.4, which expressly disclaims any renewal or extension by conduct). The structure is better than the preferred position for us: on expiry the Section 2.1 licences convert to perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free licences to Ono, and Section 13.2 gives Ono (not Array) a without-cause termination right on advance notice. No renewal exit or pricing exposure arises, so no redline is warranted.

ops.text: (x) Transition Assistance and Return of Ono Data. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Array shall (a) at Ono's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Array's then-current rates; (b) return all Data and other Confidential Information of Ono ("Customer Data") in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination; and (c) thereafter delete such Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert reciprocal Array transition-assistance and Customer Data return/deletion as new Section 14.2(a)(x)

quote: (vi) Return of Materials. Within ninety (90) days after the end of the Wind-down Period, upon request by Array, Ono shall either deliver to Array or destroy all tangible items comprising, bearing or containing trademarks of Array (including the Product Trademarks), trade names, patents, copyrights, designs, drawings, formulas or other Data, photographs, samples, literature, sales and promotional aids ("Product Materials") and Confidential Information of Array, that is in Ono's possession, subject to Ono's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes.
rationale: Article XIV is a detailed wind-down regime, but every operative transition and return obligation runs against us: we must transition studies, keep distributing, assign Regulatory Filings and hand over Data and Ono Know-How (p0659), and return or destroy Array's Materials and Confidential Information (p0662). The only mutual language is the general cooperation covenant in Section 14.2(a)(iv) (p0660), which merely transitions the Product back to Array. Nothing obliges Array to give us transition assistance or to return, delete and certify deletion of our Data and Confidential Information, so the rule's clause is absent. We therefore insert a reciprocal Section 14.2(a)(x) at the preferred level: up to six (6) months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter.

ops.text: 18.15 Insurance. Array shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance (including product liability and contractual liability coverage) of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Array processes Ono Confidential Information or personal data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Array shall provide Ono with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

quote: 16.4 Allocation. In the event a claim falls with the scope of the indemnity given by each Party, any payments in connection with such claim shall be apportioned between the Parties in accordance with the degree of fault attributable to each Party.
rationale: No insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "insurance"/"insur*"/"coverage" return only Net Sales deduction items (p0101, p0102) and "insurrection" in force majeure (p0763). Article 16 (p0715–p0727) provides reciprocal indemnities, a damages disclaimer and recall allocation, and Article 18 General Provisions (p0759–p0796) contains no insurance requirement, so the indemnities from Array — who manufactures and supplies Product (Article IX), sponsors Clinical Studies and receives our Confidential Information — are unbacked by any coverage requirement. This falls below even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). We therefore insert a short Section 18.15 in the miscellaneous section at the preferred limits, noting that in a pharma licence equivalent coverage is sometimes carried under the Quality/Supply Agreements (p0772), which Array may evidence instead.

ops.text: Cap on Aggregate Liability. Except in respect of Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10, its data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2, its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Customer's payment obligations, including all amounts due under this Agreement, are not damages for purposes of the foregoing cap.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims after Section 16.5

quote: NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 16.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE AMOUNTS PAYABLE TO THIRD PARTIES UNDER THE INDEMNITIES PROVIDED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10, SECTIONS 16.1 AND 16.2 ABOVE; PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE FOREGOING LIMITATION OF LIABILITY SHALL NOT APPLY IN THE CASE OF GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
rationale: Section 16.5 (p0727) is a mutual exclusion of special, indirect, punitive, incidental and consequential damages with carve-outs for the Article 10 / Sections 16.1-16.2 indemnities and for gross negligence and willful misconduct, but no monetary aggregate cap exists anywhere in the Agreement (Section 17.3(d) at p0751 only bars the tribunal from awarding punitive or excess damages), so each Party's direct-damages liability is unlimited. That fails the fallback's material requirement of a mutual 12 months' fees cap and is materially adverse to Ono, which carries the commercialization and product-liability indemnity risk for the Ono Territory under Section 16.1. We therefore insert a new Section 16.6 at the preferred position: a mutual cap at the greater of the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP-infringement claims, and confirming Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.
